newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Part-time work drives NZ employment growth higher.
newsitem.headline: Part-time work drives NZ employment growth higher.

text.p: Part-time employment accounted for all of the 0.8 percent seasonally-adjusted employment growth in the September quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
Full time seasonally-adjusted employment fell 0.8 percent, or 10,000 people, in the September quarter. Part-time employment rose 6.7 percent (25,000 people) to reach 397,000 in the September quarter.
The seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate for the quarter was 6.3 percent, against 6.1 percent in the June quarter and 6.1 percent in the September 1995 quarter.
Seasonally-adjusted unemployment, at 115,000 people, was 4.5 percent higher than in June 1996, and 7.5 percent higher than a year ago.
The trend unemployment rate was also 6.3 percent, against 6.1 percent in June and 6.2 percent in September 1995. The number of long-term unemployed dropped 5.3 percent in the year to September.

In the year to September, seasonally-adjusted employment rose 3.7 percent to 1.702 million people. This compares with an annual rise to June and March 1996 of 3.9 percent, and an annual increase to December 1995 of 4.2 percent, indicating a slow-down in the rate of employment growth.
Seasonally-adjusted labour force participation rose to 66.4 percent in the September quarter, the highest rate recorded since the March 1987 quarter, when 66.4 percent was also recorded.
